root_cause_analysis.hypothesis: SDAA eager mode (triton interpret) causes insufficient steps for 3D large radius convergence

evidence.comparison: CUDA compiled 3D ~1000 steps/s, so SDAA eager 3D is ~70x slower

evidence.issue: Large radius (R=40) requires more steps to converge on slow hardware

evidence.description: A 10% error in dp for R=40 (due to insufficient convergence) produces intercept_frac=4.010%, matching m52

mechanism.description: The Laplace law fit (dp vs 1/R) is sensitive to the large radius data point. If R=40 hasn't fully converged, its dp value is off, which shifts the linear fit and increases the intercept fraction.

sdaa_failure.likely_cause: R=40 dp value not fully converged, causing fit deviation

inverse_analysis.conclusion: Either a -10.4% or +5.6% error in dp_40 produces the observed 4.010% intercept

option_2.name: Tighten convergence criterion
option_2.cons: May not help if already stuck in local minimum

option_4.name: Honest-FAIL documentation
option_4.change: Document as known SDAA limitation, exclude 3D from SDAA regression

proposed_fix.recommendation: Option 4 (honest-FAIL) - document as known SDAA performance limitation

conclusion: The m52 3D FAIL (intercept_fraction=4.010%) is caused by SDAA eager mode being too slow to fully converge the large radius (R=40) case within the default step limit. Perturbation analysis confirms that a ~10% error in dp for R=40 (consistent with insufficient convergence) produces the observed intercept_fraction. This is a performance limitation, not a correctness bug. Recommended action: document as honest-FAIL for SDAA 3D regression, keep 2D (which passes).
limitations: Did not run full 3D SDAA simulation to reproduce m52 failure (too slow, 1+ hour)
